title: Annotated validation and independent transfer
intro: A03 introduces one-to-one annotation matching, foreground IoU versus object F1, group-safe test partitions and biological replicates. Browser masks are synthetic; external local BBBC038/039 benchmark code supplies actual reference-image evidence.

scientific_context.caution: BBBC038 original test object micro F1 0.385 and BBBC039 original test F1 0.841 use different data and mask conventions. They do not prove user-specific exopher accuracy.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → independent Prove → delayed review; reproduce a held-out real annotation benchmark locally.

goals.title: Pixel overlap is not object accuracy
goals.why: Two touching nuclei merged into one region can still have perfect foreground pixel IoU.
explain: Binary foreground IoU discards individual object IDs.
Count distinct positive IDs separately from background.

worked_example.code:
import numpy as np
a=np.array([[0,1,1,0],[0,2,2,0]])
b=np.array([[0,9,9,0],[0,9,9,0]])
print('foreground equal:',bool(np.array_equal(a>0,b>0)),'truth objects:',len(np.unique(a[a>0])))

goals.title: Prevent group leakage before evaluation
goals.why: Images from the same experimental group can leak across training and evaluation.
explain: A random image split is not automatically specimen- or experiment-disjoint.
Groups must be verified from experimental metadata, not invented for each image.

worked_example.code:
rows=[('animal1','calibration'),('animal1','holdout')]
print('same animal in two sets is not independent:',len(set(x for x,s in rows if s=='calibration')&set(x for x,s in rows if s=='holdout'))>0)
